bone.$description: Bone — Page canvas, card surfaces, hairline dividers between sections, ghost-button borders — the lightest structural gray carries borders, surface, and the dominant background in a near-white mode

charcoal.$description: Charcoal — Primary body and heading text, nav links, footer text, filled button text — near-black for maximum legibility without the harshness of pure black

paper.$description: Paper — Card surfaces, filled button backgrounds, image overlays, reverse text on dark sections — the brightest structural white

obsidian.$description: Obsidian — Headings on light canvas where maximum contrast is required, nav background accents — used sparingly only where absolute black is needed

deep-current.$description: Deep Current — Dark feature section backgrounds (alternating bands), large image containers — the navy-black that recedes like deep ocean water

slate-depth.$description: Slate Depth — Secondary dark section background, elevated panels over Deep Current — one step lighter to layer depth within dark bands

soehne.$description: All interface type: weight 300 reserved for display headings (48–140px) to create a quiet engineering voice, 400 for body and subheadings, 500 for nav and meta, 600 for button labels. Soehne's geometric neutrality with the extreme -0.043em tracking on display sizes is the signature — it makes headlines feel architectural rather than editorial. Substitute: Inter (closest free analog with matching weights and tracking) or Untitled Sans.
